Method of Attack: Harvesting credit card details and personal information via a fake McAfee subscription renewal scam page
Collecting visitor's name, email, card number, expiration date, CVC, address, city, state, zip, and phone number through forms
Redirecting to a thank you page with a phone number to call for fake technical support
Scammers remotely connect to victim's computer pretending to assist with software installation
Stealing credit card and personal information for identity theft and unauthorized charges
Hosting and distributing unwanted software and adware that creates random executables and opens advertising redirects
Discoverer: Thomas Roccia, security researcher at McAfee Labs
Impacted Systems: Windows PCs infected by WizzCaster adware
Attack Vector: Browser-based tech support scam via fake McAfee subscription expiration page
Remote connection initiated by scammers after victim calls provided phone number
Adware installed on infected PCs that auto-starts and opens malicious advertisements
Indicators of Compromise: WizzCaster adware creating random named executables
Affiliate URLs redirecting to McAfee site
Malware hashes identified by Thomas Roccia
